title: Indian Airlines Extend Saudi Flight Cancellations Through October 15
excerpt: IndiGo, Air India and Air India Express have pushed Riyadh suspensions to October 14–15 as King Khalid International stays closed after Houthi attacks — with full refunds on offer for affected passengers.
body:
• India's airlines have extended Riyadh cancellations again. IndiGo has cancelled all flights to Riyadh and Dammam through October 15, while Air India has suspended flights through October 15 and Air India Express through October 14 — an extension of the suspensions first announced on October 8.
  • The extension follows a weekend escalation. Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport has been closed since a Saturday attack that killed 13 people, and Houthi rebels have claimed ballistic-missile strikes on the airport.
  • What to do if you're booked to fly: do not head to the airport — check your flight status in the airline's app or website first. Air India and Air India Express are offering full refunds to affected passengers, and Air India Express is also offering free rescheduling; refund and rebooking policies vary by airline, so confirm yours before buying a replacement ticket. For essential travel, consider routing through Dubai or Doha on unaffected carriers.
  • The disruption is now global. Lufthansa Group flights to Riyadh are suspended through October 16, Air France-KLM through the end of October, Etihad's Saudi services through October 13, and Singapore Airlines has postponed its Riyadh launch to March 2027.

Opening: the extension travelers feared

Indian airlines have pushed their Saudi Arabia cancellations further out, extending the suspension of flights to Riyadh well beyond the initial October 9–10 window. IndiGo, India's largest carrier, has cancelled all services to Riyadh and Dammam through October 15. Air India has suspended flights to and from the Saudi capital through October 15, and Air India Express through October 14. The extensions follow a weekend of attacks on King Khalid International Airport that left the airport closed and forced airlines across the world to reroute or ground their Saudi operations.

Context & Background: how the disruption escalated

The crisis began on October 8, when Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis claimed a ballistic-missile strike on King Khalid International Airport and renewed threats against airlines using Saudi airspace. Smoke was seen rising from a stationary aircraft at the airport, and Saudi authorities said three people had been killed in strikes on Riyadh airport and Abha airport earlier that week. In the first wave of suspensions, IndiGo cancelled Riyadh flights through October 9, while Air India and Akasa Air cancelled through October 10 — one Air India flight from Delhi to Riyadh even turned back mid-route.

Then came the weekend escalation: the airport has been closed since a Saturday attack that killed 13 people, and total cancellations at the airport reached 293, per aviation data trackers. The UK Foreign Office has advised against all but essential travel to Riyadh province and several other Saudi regions.

Impact & Analysis: which airlines, which routes, until when

The Indian carriers are far from alone. Lufthansa Group has cancelled all flights to Riyadh through October 16 across its airlines. Air France-KLM extended an earlier suspension of services to and from the Saudi capital to the end of the month. Etihad Airways suspended all flights to Saudi Arabia until October 13. Singapore Airlines postponed the launch of its Riyadh service to March 28, 2027. Emirates, flydubai, Turkish Airlines, and Pakistan International Airlines have cancelled or suspended select Riyadh services, and Riyadh Air itself saw cancellations at its home hub.

Both Air India and Air India Express are offering full refunds to affected passengers, and Air India Express is additionally offering complimentary rescheduling. Other carriers' policies vary — check directly with your airline rather than assuming the same terms.

Diaspora Angle

Saudi Arabia hosts one of the largest Indian expatriate populations in the world, and October is a heavy travel month for family visits and job rotations. If you or a family member is affected: (1) check flight status on your airline's app or website before going to the airport; (2) claim the full refund or free rescheduling your airline is offering — do not accept a paid rebooking without first asking about waiver options; (3) if travel is urgent, look at Dubai or Doha connections on carriers still operating, since the suspension is route-specific, not a blanket regional shutdown; (4) monitor your airline's travel advisories and the Indian Embassy in Riyadh's guidance, as suspension dates keep shifting.

What's Next

Flights can't resume until King Khalid International reopens and carriers are cleared to return. With Air France-KLM out through month's end and Singapore Airlines deferring to next March, carriers expect weeks, not days, of disruption — expect further rolling extensions, and check your booking's status daily.

Sources: Reuters, Mint, FTN News.
